official.deadline_note: The portfolio publishes no single deadline. Published dates: Call 2026-2027 for reimbursement of study materials, initial deadline 00:00 on 1 March 2027 and final deadline 23:59 on 31 March 2027; Wanted the Best 2026-2027, deadline October 30, 2026; International Post-degree Scholarship Call 2026, deadline September 16, 2026; 100 scholarships for students with care responsibilities or in vulnerable circumstances, 23:59 on May 29, 2026; Rieti campus scholarships for foreign students (a.y. 2024/25 edition), 14 November 2024. Student-collaboration calls are usually published from September each year and must allow at least 30 consecutive calendar days for applications.
official.application_cycle: Academic year 2026/2027 - rolling portfolio of calls published across the year
official.status_note: The official Scholarships index is live and lists open calls for 2026/2027. The 2026-2027 reimbursement of study materials call is currently open (initial deadline 1 March 2027, final deadline 31 March 2027) and a new call for accommodation at Sapienza University Residences is listed. The International Post-degree Scholarship Call 2026 closed on 16 September 2026 and the 100-scholarship call closed on 29 May 2026; the index states that scholarships and awards are granted throughout the year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Only the Rieti campus scholarship for foreign students states tuition coverage: winners are exempted from payment of university tuition fees and must pay EUR 30.00 as a single contribution, while stamp duty and the Lazio regional tax remain due. No other scheme on the Scholarships index publishes tuition coverage; general fee relief runs instead through ISEE-based exemptions and reductions, with tuition payable in three instalments of 30%, 35% and 35% (5 November 2026, 17 December 2026, 25 March 2027).
benefits: International Post-degree Scholarship: EUR 1,290.00 per month, for a minimum of 6 months to a maximum of 12 months, for courses or advanced training activities at international university institutions; exempt from Irpef treatment under Article 4 of Law 476/84
Wanted the Best: 85 two-year scholarships of EUR 3,000.00 per year (gross of the statutory withholdings paid by the student and net of those paid by the University)
International Thesis Scholarship: EUR 2,821.00 gross (Regional Income Tax included) for the whole internship, conducted for at least two consecutive months

Student-collaboration scholarships: EUR 1,295.00 tax-free for 150 hours of paid activity; the fee for support activities for students with disabilities and with Specific Learning Difficulties is EUR 1,500.00 tax-free

Reimbursement of study materials: one reimbursement per recipient for a maximum amount of EUR 500.00, as a detailed refund of expenses actually incurred; 100 scholarships of EUR 1,000.00 each (before tax deductions) for students with care responsibilities or in vulnerable circumstances

Rieti campus scholarships for foreign students: EUR 7,098.62 per year (EUR 6,542.51 gross IRPEF plus EUR 556.11 IRAP) for three years, plus exemption from university tuition fees and a single EUR 30.00 contribution
eligibility: Enrolment in a Bachelor's, Master's or single-cycle degree programme at Sapienza University of Rome - the collaboration scholarships are reserved exclusively for Sapienza-enrolled students

International Post-degree Scholarship: holders of a Master's degree, single-cycle Master's degree or equivalent awarded by Sapienza, who are 28 years old or younger by the announcement of the call and graduated within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the announcement
International Thesis Scholarship: students properly enrolled at least in the Master's degree first year (two-year duration), or in the last or second-to-last year of a single cycle degree

Wanted the Best: students who obtained a first degree in other Italian universities than Sapienza with a grade between 105/110 and 110/110 cum laude, enrolling in a Master's degree programme at Sapienza in 2026/2027
Rieti campus scholarships for foreign students: students with non-Italian citizenship resident abroad, enrolled in Sustainable building engineering at the Polo Universitario Interateneo di Rieti

Student-collaboration scholarships: students enrolled from the second or third year up to the first year outside the course, who have obtained at least 2/5 of the ECTS required by their training course with reference to the preceding academic year
requirements: Candidates for the International Post-degree Scholarship may submit only one application, relating to a single CUN disciplinary area corresponding to their degree class
An official acceptance and/or invitation letter and/or declaration of availability to admission from a hosting foreign institution or from a foreign supervisor, drafted on headed and certified paper

The application for the International Post-degree Scholarship must be drafted in PDF format according to the model attached to the call and sent exclusively by certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it
Student-collaboration applications are submitted through the Borsecoll platform, after reading the application requisites in the individual calls
International Thesis Scholarships are awarded by each faculty through its own call and applications are made at the faculty presidencies
For non-Italian citizens under the International Post-degree Scholarship, the host institution must be located in a country other than their country of origin
documents: Certification released by the foreign institution, drafted according to a certified format with the institution's official signature and stamp, containing the name of the course, its internal structure and respective duration, or the programme of activities to be completed
Self-declaration of publications and previously attained titles, drafted in PDF according to the format required by the call
Translation into Italian of the documentation released by the foreign institution, only if the document was initially released in a language other than English
Application form compiled and signed on the model attached to the relevant call

For admitted candidates: a self-declaration of possessing the compulsory requirements stated in the call, and a new certification released by the international institution indicating the starting and final date of the specialisation activity
selection_criteria: International Post-degree Scholarship: a selection process based on qualifications and exams; a Selection Committee nominated for each disciplinary area attributes up to 100 points, with up to 50 points for the degree final grade, previously attained titles and publications, and up to 50 points for the interview

Suitable candidates are contacted for an interview to verify the level of preparation in the selected disciplinary field and the knowledge of the language requested by the hosting foreign institution; a score under 35 points is considered not sufficient

Student-collaboration scholarships: the merit score adds the weighted average of the marks of the exams taken in the course currently attended (30 with honours counts as 30.10) and the ratio between credits obtained and credits foreseen, multiplied by 30, reduced by one point for each year out-of-course or repeating
Exams and credits obtained at foreign universities can be declared only if already validated or recognised at Sapienza within the current study course
Wanted the Best is a competition based on qualifications, with eligibility in article 2 and the application procedure in article 3 of the call
coverage: Monthly support for courses or advanced training activities at international university institutions outside Italy (International Post-degree Scholarship)
Detailed refund of expenses actually incurred for educational materials purchased between January 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027, up to EUR 500.00 per recipient

Payment for 150 hours of collaboration with university structures such as libraries, museums and sports facilities, laboratories, multimedia classrooms, promotion of the educational offer, reception and information services, support services for students with disabilities, and tutoring

Funding for thesis research conducted abroad for at least two consecutive months at institutions, companies, foreign or community companies, or supranational and international institutions of higher scientific and cultural level
Exemption from university tuition fees and a single EUR 30.00 contribution for winners of the Rieti campus scholarship, plus accommodation places in Sapienza University Residences
Regional scholarships and housing assigned by Disco Lazio, the regional agency for the right to study, through a competitive selection process
application_method: PEC-only submission for the International Post-degree Scholarship, in PDF on the model attached to the call, sent to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it
Online application through the Borsecoll platform for student-collaboration scholarships
Application at the faculty presidencies for International Thesis Scholarships, each awarded by its faculty
Calls, forms and rankings are published on the Amministrazione trasparente / Transparency Portal
Regional right-to-study benefits are requested directly through Disco Lazio's competitive selection
official.application_route: Apply to the individual call rather than a central office: each scheme publishes its own call on the Amministrazione trasparente portal or a faculty portal, and submission runs through PEC (post-degree), the Borsecoll platform (collaboration) or the faculty presidency (international thesis).
official.citizenship_residency: Set per individual call. Most schemes require current enrolment at Sapienza on a degree programme, irrespective of citizenship. The Rieti campus scholarship is reserved for non-Italian citizens resident abroad. The International Post-degree Scholarship is open to Sapienza graduates of any citizenship, but for non-Italian citizens the host institution must be in a country other than their country of origin.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible for several schemes. The Scholarships index is published in English and the Rieti campus scholarship is reserved for non-Italian citizens resident abroad; the International Thesis and International Post-degree Scholarships and the page on Scholarships for Meritorious Students from Italian and International Universities explicitly address international candidates. Regional benefits through Disco Lazio are likewise open to international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Some schemes are field-restricted: the Rieti campus scholarship is limited to Sustainable building engineering at the Polo Universitario Interateneo di Rieti (with further Rieti calls for health professions and for economics and engineering); International Thesis Scholarships are administered by each faculty; IUPALS is a CRUI/MAECI project for Palestinian students; and #100ragazzeSTEM is a Sapienza scholarship for outstanding women in STEM. The collaboration and 100-scholarship schemes are not field-restricted.
official.research_requirement: The International Post-degree Scholarship supports third-cycle study programmes or postgraduate advanced training activities abroad and requires an official acceptance, invitation or declaration of availability from a hosting foreign institution or foreign supervisor, with one application per CUN disciplinary area. The International Thesis Scholarship requires part of the thesis research to be conducted abroad for at least two consecutive months at an institution of higher scientific and cultural level.
official.duration: Varies by scheme: International Post-degree Scholarship a minimum of 6 to a maximum of 12 months; Wanted the Best two-year scholarships; International Thesis Scholarship at least two consecutive months; student-collaboration 150 hours per academic year; study-materials purchases between January 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027; Rieti campus scholarships three years.
official.description: Sapienza Universita di Roma publishes a portfolio of scholarships and grants covering reimbursement of study materials, accommodation in university residences, international thesis work, post-degree study abroad, paid student collaboration and support for students with care responsibilities or in vulnerable circumstances. Regional right-to-study benefits are administered separately by Disco Lazio through a competitive selection. The university's Scholarships page is the authoritative index and states that scholarships and awards are granted throughout the year.

applicant_utility.summary: Sapienza does not run one scholarship you apply to once - it runs a menu of separately-timed calls, and almost every one of them requires you to already be a Sapienza student or a Sapienza graduate. For a prospective Master's applicant the figures that matter are EUR 3,000 a year for two years under Wanted the Best (deadline 30 October 2026, but restricted to graduates of other Italian universities), EUR 2,821 gross for a thesis period abroad, and EUR 1,295 tax-free for 150 hours of collaboration work. International students should treat the Disco Lazio regional route and the Rieti campus scholarship - EUR 7,098.62 a year plus tuition exemption for non-Italian citizens - as the only two routes that genuinely touch fees. Work to the calendar rather than a single deadline: the post-degree call closed on 16 September 2026, the 100-scholarship call closed on 29 May 2026, and the study-materials reimbursement call stays open until 1 March 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A student already enrolled, or about to enrol, at Sapienza who will monitor the Transparency Portal every month rather than an external applicant hunting for one large fully funded award.
application_readiness_checklist: Sort your credentials before any call opens: a PEC address is mandatory for the post-degree scholarship, and SPID or CIE are needed for Infostud and the Borsecoll platform.
Obtain an ISEE declaration if you want any fee reduction - if the value is not in Infostud by 17 December 2026 you pay tuition at the maximum rate, and filing late costs EUR 50 to EUR 100 on top.

Secure the foreign host before applying for the post-degree or thesis scholarship: you need an acceptance, invitation or availability letter on the host's letterhead, signed and stamped, naming the course, its structure and duration.

Convert foreign exams and credits into the Italian 30-point scale before filling in a collaboration application - Sapienza requires manual conversion, and a career that cannot be converted forces you to sit the SAT.
Keep itemised receipts for study material bought between 1 January 2026 and 31 March 2027; the EUR 500 is a detailed refund of expenses actually incurred, not a lump sum, and you only ever get one.
Diary the fee instalments (5 November 2026, 17 December 2026, 25 March 2027) alongside the scholarship deadlines, because late payment carries EUR 65 rising to EUR 130 after 60 days.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a CUN disciplinary area that does not match your degree class - the application is rejected outright as incongruous or inconsistent.

Being over the age limit: the post-degree scholarship requires you to be 28 or younger by the announcement of the call, and to have graduated in the last viable session of the preceding academic year.
Sending the post-degree application by ordinary email or a non-certified address; only PEC submission to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it is accepted.
Claiming foreign exams or credits that were never formally recognised at Sapienza - they are excluded from the merit score entirely.

Holding another scholarship during the post-degree period abroad; PhD students with a PhD scholarship must renounce it, and specialisation-school students cannot combine their school scholarship with this one.
Exceeding the annual income ceiling set out in the call for the calendar year in which the scholarship is held, or missing the September window for collaboration calls.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Rome, flights, relocation and installation abroad for the mobility scholarships, the EUR 30 single contribution plus stamp duty and the Lazio regional tax that survive even the Rieti tuition exemption, tuition fees for anyone not exempt or ISEE-reduced, and the cost of Italian translations and certified copies of foreign documents.
document_audit: The foreign acceptance letter must be on headed paper with the institution's official signature and stamp and must state the course name, internal structure and duration, or the programme of the specialisation activity - a generic acceptance email will not pass.
Publications and titles must be self-declared on the exact PDF model attached to the call, not on a free-format CV.
Admitted candidates must later produce a fresh certificate from the host institution with the actual start and end dates, so the host relationship has to survive until after the interview.

For collaboration grants every exam and credit, including those from previous or recognised foreign careers, must be declared exactly as recorded, because the merit score is recomputed from your own entries.
Foreign qualification marks and credits have to be manually converted into the Italian system before submission, and an unconvertible career triggers a mandatory SAT result.
alerts: There is no single Sapienza deadline. The post-degree call is published every year in April/May and this cycle closed 16 September 2026 - mark April-May rather than waiting for a summer alert.
Scholarship payments are suspended in December and January for Sapienza's year-end closing, so budget two months without cash.

The second tuition instalment falls on 17 December 2026 and the third on 25 March 2027, while the study-materials reimbursement deadline is 1 March 2027 and its final deadline 31 March 2027 - March is the month where fee and scholarship deadlines collide.

Wanted the Best is advertised for graduates of Italian and international universities, but the published eligibility is a first degree from an Italian university other than Sapienza with at least 105/110, so most international applicants will not qualify.
Incoming exchange students under Sapienza's bilateral agreements receive no scholarship from the university at all.
The Rieti foreign-students call linked from the index is the a.y. 2024/25 edition (deadline 14 November 2024), so confirm a new edition exists before relying on the EUR 7,098.62 figure.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch the Transparency Portal for your scheme's own call, submit on that call's format by PEC, Borsecoll or the faculty presidency, then await a merit ranking plus interview (post-degree) or a merit ranking alone (collaboration) before payment.
